title: Boundaries, failures and recovery
goal: Distinguish malformed records, unknown IDs, invalid commands and report errors by status, stream and artifact.

prerequisites.text: You will need inventory_find and the checks for fopen and fclose. Start in a fresh working folder.

terms.title: Validation before commands
terms.definition: The entire input file is validated before reading the first command.

terms.title: First failure
terms.definition: The first recorded cause of termination. A close error does not overwrite a previously recorded write failure.

sections.title: The cause of a stop depends on the stage
paragraphs: If the file repeats an ID, the quantity update has no unique row. Load and validate the file first. Check format, uniqueness and capacity before appending each record. No command has run yet.

Input file errors go to stderr with status 1. A syntactically valid command for an unknown ID writes missing to stdout and continues. Bad command syntax writes invalid to stdout and stops with status 2. Later stdin lines are skipped.

A directory occupying the report path leaves stdout empty, exits with status 3 and keeps keep.txt. The native fixture rejects fopen with open-report-error. In Clang/WASI the failure is observed when buffered output is closed: close-report-error. Check both stages and print reported only after a successful fclose.

sections.title: Two matching IDs stop the program before any commands
paragraphs: The file contains 10 with quantity 5, followed by 0010 with quantity 0. Both IDs parse to the number 10. In the walkthrough, report would write example-summary.tsv. Check for it to see whether execution reached the commands.
steps: The first record loads. Before the second append, inventory_find sees the existing ID.
The input stream closes. Stderr has duplicate-id plus LF, status is 1 and stdout is empty.
A fresh directory has no example-summary.tsv because writing the report never started.

sections.title: Where to look for the cause
paragraphs: For a fclose compiler diagnostic, check the FILE * argument. At runtime, read stdout alongside stderr and the exit status. Empty stdout, nonempty stderr and status 1 place the failure before command processing.

When a directory occupies the report path, an I/O error can appear during open or close depending on the environment. Check the stream and message for that environment, status 3, and the absence of a new file.

sections.title: Test your prediction with a new input
paragraphs: A report issued before an invalid command can remain. In a separate run compare two command orders. Distinguish no new report from deletion of an earlier report.

For your own runs, replace records.tsv in two clean copies. Write two distinct valid IDs with a quantity for each. Use one syntactically valid command for an absent ID in the first copy and a malformed command in the second. Follow each command with report. Predict stdout, stderr, exit status, and the presence of a new file for each run.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Compare the listed C17 rules with their use in this project.

selfcheck.prompt: In a fresh folder with valid records, stdin contains set 20 10000 and report. What do you observe?
options: ok followed by an empty report.
feedback: The quantity is out of range. Processing stopped before report.
Argument validation happens before a record is looked up.

selfcheck.prompt: The record and the report command are valid. A directory containing keep.txt occupies summary.tsv. What distinguishes this failure from a data error?
options: invalid in stdout, status 2 and an empty directory.
Browser stderr is close-report-error, status is 3 and keep.txt is unchanged.
feedback: Uniqueness errors are found when loading the input.
This is an output failure. The native fixture detects it when opening, while the verified Clang/WASI run detects it on close. Both paths return 3 and retain keep.txt.

selfcheck.prompt: Why does the absence of summary.tsv in this example only establish the ordering of events? What if a valid report ran before the bad command?
selfcheck.feedback: A fresh folder and no report call explain the absence of a file. A previously successful report remains because the invalid command does not open it.

cases.label: An earlier report survives an error

practice.title: Guard the report from a duplicate record
practice.task: The training log repeats ID 32. The starter omits the uniqueness check. Add it before appending to the array. Test the controls for an unknown ID, an invalid quantity, excess capacity and a report open failure.

steps.action: Run the starter against the duplicate using report.
steps.why: Two rows with the same ID make the report ambiguous.
steps.expected: The broken version prints reported and writes duplicate rows.

steps.action: Check for a repeated ID before appending the row. Rerun this case and the other controls.
steps.why: Status 1 should remain distinct from command errors and the report open failure.
steps.expected: A duplicate leaves stdout empty, prints duplicate-id to stderr and exits 1. A name conflict exits 3 and prints close-report-error in Code Studio. The native Clang fixture detects it on open.

criteria: A duplicate or a 65th unique row leaves no report. Stderr distinguishes duplicate-id from capacity-error.
An unknown ID yields missing and execution continues. An invalid quantity gives invalid and status 2 before report executes.
The summary.tsv directory and keep.txt stay unchanged. A name conflict leaves stdout empty and exits 3. Code Studio reports close-report-error; the verified native run reports open-report-error.
practice.hint: Find the state where the program can check the new ID before adding its row. What must happen before the first stdin command if the ID is a duplicate?

exercises.title: One more check
exercises.task: In a fresh run invert the order of report and an invalid command. Record when the file exists and identify the failure by exit status.
criteria: Write your prediction before running. Compare stdout, stderr, status and files.

teaching.scene: Before inventory starts, check that one malformed record stops loading before commands run. Distinguish loading, command, and report failures by their streams and exit status.

predict.prompt: The example has IDs 10 and 0010 and stdin contains report. Will report run? Predict stdout, stderr, the exit status, and whether a new file appears.
predict.answer: Both spellings parse as numeric ID 10. Loading stops at the duplicate before the command loop. stdout is empty, stderr contains duplicate-id, exit status is 1, and no new report is created.

apply.prompt: Use the valid input with 10 TAB 5 and 20 TAB 0. Run report, set 20 10000, then report again. Is a report left behind, and was it generated twice?
apply.answer: The first report writes the original quantities 5 and 0 and prints reported. set rejects the five-digit quantity, prints invalid, and exits 2. The second report is never reached, and the first file remains in the run results.

practice.strategy: Sketch the checks for one record in order: syntax, uniqueness, capacity. Record four observations separately for duplicate ID 32, a malformed command, a missing item, and a blocked report path.
practice.diagnosis: If duplicate ID 32 still gives reported, check whether the insertion happens before the uniqueness test. If a missing ID stops a valid command sequence, distinguish the normal missing response from a command failure.

syntax.explanation: Append only after validation. Short-circuiting in the || chain protects later parsing operations. The else if branches distinguish a duplicate from a capacity failure.
syntax.mistake: Do not check for duplicates after increasing count. The record you just inserted would already be in the search range. Keep the different stages of failure in separate tests.
